title: Finite diagonal from an affine adequate moduli space
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $\mathcal X$ a finite-type algebraic stack over $k$, and $\phi:\mathcal X\to Y$ an adequate moduli space [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space] with $Y$ an affine $k$-scheme. Suppose the diagonal $\Delta_{\mathcal X/k}:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X$ is quasi-finite and separated, meaning that after scheme charts it is finite type with finite geometric fibres and separated. Then $\Delta_{\mathcal X/k}$ is finite. In particular, the inertia morphism $I_{\mathcal X}\to\mathcal X$ is finite; here $I_{\mathcal X}=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X}\mathcal X$ with both maps to the product the diagonal, so its objects over an object $x$ are automorphisms of $x$. Finite for a representable morphism means finite after scheme charts, in [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; finite type uses [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Theorem 8.3.2, implication (3) to (1), especially its proof for separated Y concluding that the diagonal is finite, printed pp.39--40; Lemma 8.3.1. The statement keeps the affine-target hypothesis needed for that stronger conclusion. Read arXiv:1005.2398v3 online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal V=\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X$ and $B=\Gamma(\mathcal V,\mathcal O_{\mathcal V})$. Apply [lem-sfb-adequate-product-affinization] to the given $\phi$ and affine $Y$. This supplies an adequate moduli space $\psi:\mathcal V\to Z=\operatorname{Spec}B$; it imposes no extra hypothesis on $\Delta_{\mathcal X/k}$.

source.place: Theorem 8.3.2, product and relative spectrum in the proof of (3) implies (1), pp.39--40; online arXiv:1005.2398v3, local PDF WANTED

proof.text: Write $A=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$, so $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$. The structure-sheaf isomorphism in [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space] identifies $\phi^*:A\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(\mathcal X,\mathcal O_{\mathcal X})$. Define $r=(\phi^*)^{-1}\Delta^*:B\to A$ and $s=\mathrm{pr}_1^*\phi^*:A\to B$. Since $\mathrm{pr}_1\Delta=\mathrm{id}$, we have $rs=\mathrm{id}_A$, so $r$ is surjective. Thus, for every $a\in A$, the monic polynomial $T-s(a)\in B[T]$ vanishes at $a$ under $r$, and $r$ is integral. By the affine definition [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $g=\operatorname{Spec}r:Y\to Z$ is integral. Contravariant functoriality of Spec [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives $\psi\Delta=g\phi$: on an affine smooth chart of $\mathcal X$ the two maps to $\operatorname{Spec}B$ induce the same ring map, namely restriction of $\Delta^*$, hence agree; these equalities are compatible on chart overlaps.

source.place: Affine-target version of the integral lower arrow in Theorem 8.3.2; explicit ring retraction written by Q95; online arXiv:1005.2398v3, local PDF WANTED

proof.text: The hypotheses on $\mathcal X/k$ and its diagonal are exactly those of [lem-sfb-stack-diagonal-closed-points]. Hence $\Delta$ sends closed points of $|\mathcal X|$ to closed points of $|\mathcal V|$. This supplies the closed-point condition; it is not inferred merely from quasi-finiteness.

source.place: Theorem 8.3.2, closed-point sentence, pp.39--40; online arXiv:1005.2398v3, local PDF WANTED

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-adequate-integral-comparison-finite] with $\mathcal U=\mathcal X$, $\mathcal V=\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X$, $p=\phi$, $q=\psi$, $P=Y$, $Q=Z$, $f=\Delta$ and the $g$ of step 2. Both stacks are of finite type over $k$: $\mathcal X$ by hypothesis, and $\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X$ because the product of two smooth finite-type scheme atlases of $\mathcal X$ is a smooth finite-type atlas of it and finitely many affine charts cover it. Both vertical maps are adequate moduli spaces, the square commutes by step 2, and $g$ is integral. The stack diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces by the definition of algebraic stack; its quasi-finiteness and separatedness are assumed in the item. Step 3 proves the remaining closed-point condition. The criterion therefore makes $\Delta_{\mathcal X/k}$ finite.

source.place: Lemma 8.3.1 and its application in Theorem 8.3.2, pp.39--40; online arXiv:1005.2398v3, local PDF WANTED

proof.text: For any scheme $T\to\mathcal X$, associativity of 2-fibre products identifies $I_{\mathcal X}\times_{\mathcal X}T$ with $T\times_{\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X}\mathcal X$, where $T\to\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X$ is the composite through $\Delta$. Since $\Delta$ is finite, its defining scheme-base-change test says that this is a scheme finite over $T$ in [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Thus every scheme test of $I_{\mathcal X}\to\mathcal X$ is finite, which is precisely the required finiteness of inertia.
